dimensions.assessment: Affects United States persons and individuals in the U.S. targeted by foreign government repression, as well as DHS, intelligence community, and law enforcement personnel.
dimensions.evidence: action of a foreign government or an agent of a foreign government that... occurs, in whole or in part, in the United States; or is committed against a United States person.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a specialized federal working group for intelligence analysis, information sharing, and annual reporting without altering criminal statutes.
dimensions.evidence: There is established a Working Group, to be known as the 'Transnational Repression Working Group'... within the Department

dimensions.assessment: The source authorizes the working group and research activities but does not specify dollar amounts for appropriations.
Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to create a new section establishing the working group, director position, staffing requirements, and research mandates.
dimensions.evidence: Subtitle H of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 451 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following new section

dimensions.assessment: Includes a sunset provision terminating the Working Group seven years after enactment, with annual reports required during that period.
dimensions.evidence: The Working Group shall terminate on the date that is seven years after the date of the enactment of this section.

missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budgetary allocations required to operate the working group.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill authorizes a dedicated Transnational Repression Working Group within the Department of Homeland Security to monitor and analyze foreign transnational repression threats against individuals in the U.S., conduct research, share information with fusion centers, and submit annual reports to Congress.
